interest: SCAP's 1948 quarantine rules included aircraft disinsectization and a ban on importing psittacine birds.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file (894.1246/7-2948) from the U.S. State Department decimal central files contains Despatch No. 475, dated July 29, 1948, from the Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo to the Department of State, together with an intelligence dissemination copy and its primary enclosure: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) Circular No. 9, dated March 29, 1948. Circular No. 9, issued by command of General Douglas MacArthur, establishes comprehensive foreign quarantine regulations for occupied Japan governing all incoming and outgoing surface vessels and aircraft—both military and civil—as well as their passengers, crews, and cargoes across the four main islands of Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, and Kyushu, and outlying occupation-controlled islands. Rescinding Circular No. 10 of October 28, 1946, the regulations delegate implementation to the Commanding General of the Eighth Army utilizing Japanese agencies, mandate vaccination requirements (smallpox and typhoid), define strict isolation and quarantine protocols for major communicable diseases (cholera, plague, yellow fever, louse-borne typhus, and smallpox), enforce insect and rodent disinfestation, regulate the transport of human remains and animals (including a total embargo on psittacine birds), and align occupation procedures with the International Sanitary Conventions of 1926 and 1944.

subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (by command of General Douglas MacArthur; Paul J. Mueller, Chief of Staff; R. M. Levy, Adjutant General)
subfiles.summary: Circular No. 9 of March 29, 1948, rescinds Circular No. 10 of October 28, 1946, and establishes detailed foreign quarantine procedures for the four main islands of Japan (Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu) and outlying islands under occupation control. It places operational responsibility on the Commanding General of the Eighth Army, who is authorized to establish quarantine stations at designated ports of entry and exit utilizing appropriate Japanese agencies and quarantine officers. The circular mandates vaccination against smallpox and typhoid for incoming travelers, sets rigorous vessel inspection and disinfestation requirements (including rat guards, trapping, fumigation, and aircraft disinsectization using aerosol bombs), and specifies clinical quarantine and isolation measures for five major quarantinable diseases: cholera, plague, yellow fever, louse-borne typhus, and smallpox. Special provisions also govern the shipment of embalmed human remains, strictly regulate animal imports, completely prohibit psittacine birds, and incorporate the provisions of the International Sanitary Conventions of 1926 and 1944.
